items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Dominique Cravic与Les Primitifs du futur的第五张作品，由地下漫画家Robert Crumb绘制封面，延续了乐队自1986年以来的复古拼贴路线。27首短曲以法国bal-musette手风琴为核心，融合拉格泰姆、jug band、French chanson、skiffle及各种被遗忘的老风格，使用手风琴、萨克斯、木琴、单簧管、班卓琴、尤克里里、特雷门琴、夏威夷吉他、风笛及音乐锯等古董乐器。Cravic的念白式演唱模仿Maurice Chevalier的市井气质。曲目涵盖1925年经典《Ukulele Lady》以及对2020年去世的法国抵抗运动女歌手Juliette Gréco的致敬。整张专辑像从阁楼里翻出78转唱片重新演绎，由七十多岁的乐手以认真态度呈现旧时代的音乐考古。

items._cn_summary: 柏林艺术家Laurentius前往土耳其一座洞穴教堂进行实地录音，将空间声学特性转化为专辑的核心素材。录音过程中的失误、回声与粗糙质感被视为作品不可分割的组成部分，而非需要修饰的瑕疵。这种创作方式强调环境与声音之间的直接关系，录音地点本身成为乐器的延伸。从有限的文字描述来看，作品应属于氛围与田野录音交叉的实验领域，洞穴的空间声学为声音增添了独特的混响特征与人文地理色彩。整体内容偏新闻性质，乐评深度有限，对具体的创作手法、声音设计、音乐结构等信息交代不足，难以全面评估其艺术价值。

items.body: [PLAYLIST] Kurator Mike Patricola und das Label Smiling C – das Team hinter Voice of Love – sind zurück. Pipe Dreams heißt die neue Compilation, die am 23. Oktober erscheinen wird. Sie enthält 19 vergessene Songs, aufgenommen zwischen Ende der 1970er und Mitte der 1980er, die – nun ja – nah am Wasser gebaut sind. Wortwörtlich. Seite A klassischer Yacht Rock, Seite B Surf-Disco, Seite C zeigt intimere »tropische Troubadoure«, Seite D schließt die Klammer mit Yacht-Rock. Not Only Surfin‘ U.S.A Die versammelten Interpret:innen kommen nicht nur aus den USA, sondern auch aus Australien, Japan, Kanada, Frankreich, von den Bahamas oder von Hawaii. Die Compilation zeigt Yacht Rock nicht als eine auf Kalifornien begrenzte, sondern als globale Ästhetik. Der Japaner Twin Cosmos legt auf »Coconuts Wind« eine Lennon erinnernde Melodie in eine lauwarme Meeresbrise. Pierre Rochette aus Montréal träumt sich mit afrikanischen Rhythmen und Disco-Gitarren-Grooves »On The Beach«. Miles Corbin Rick Sharp Twin Cosmos Die auf schwarzem Vinyl gepresste Schallplatte erscheint in einem luxuriösen, gestanzten Gatefold-Cover mit Spotlackierung und ist auf dem europäischen Festland exklusiv bei HHV erhältlich. Das Artwork stammt von Charles Bals und basiert auf dem Foto »Breaking Wave« von Lex Thompson. Im HHV Shop kaufenV.A.Pipe Dreams HHV EU Exclusive Black Vinyl Editionab 47.99€

items._cn_summary: Smiling C厂牌与策展人Mike Patricola合作推出的合辑《Pipe Dreams》，收录19首1970年代末至1980年代中期的遗珠作品。唱片以四面结构组织：A面为经典游艇摇滚，B面为冲浪迪斯科，C面呈现热带行吟歌手的私密质感，D面以游艇摇滚收束。来自澳大利亚、日本、加拿大、法国、巴哈马和夏威夷的艺术家参与其中，打破了该类型以加州为中心的地域局限，呈现为一种跨国美学。制作采用黑胶实体，配以烫金封面与局部UV工艺。这是一张定位明确的复古类型合辑，文字内容更接近唱片发行资讯而非深度评论，所涉风格与实验、前卫、当代古典等方向距离较远。

items.body: Paulina Fae has released Lilac Cat, a six-song ethereal dream pop EP, on Projekt Records on 18 September 2026. The EP is out now digitally, streaming or pay-what-you-can on Bandcamp, and is also available on Spotify and YouTube Music. The six songs on ‘Lilac Cat’ The tracklist runs “Lilac Cat,” “Spinning Lullabies,” “In Veils of Spiderwebs,” “Aetheris,” “Wandermind” and “Noctivine.” Projekt Records describes the EP as a collection of “ethereal dream pop and otherworldly reverie,” moving from the “galaxy-eyed whimsy” of the title track and the “dream-jazz sounds” of “Spinning Lullabies” to the “faery-like currents” of “Aetheris,” with songs that wander through misty forests, celestial worlds and violet dreams carried by ethereal vocals. Lilac Cat by Paulina Fae ‘Lilac Cat’ follows Paulina Fae’s 2025 album “Ghostbirds,” a 10-song collection built around minimalist piano and soft, misty vocals, and continues her run of releases on Projekt Records, the label she has recorded for since 2012. About Paulina Fae Paulina Fae records under her given name, Paulina Cassidy, and has also used the name Polly Fae across her catalogue. Born in Ontario, Canada, she is a visual artist and songwriter based in Chattanooga, Tennessee, known for illustrated tarot and oracle decks including the Paulina Tarot, the Joie de Vivre Tarot, Witchlings, Pixiekins, Spiritsong Tarot and Phantasma Tarot, and for books such as “The Secret Language of Trees,” “Kindred Guardians” and “Mortimer: A Cat’s Journey in the Afterlife.” She self-released her earliest music as Paulina Cassidy through Ulaluma Productions, starting with “Bloodroots” in 2010, followed by “Time Traveler” in 2011 and “Lost in Oz” in 2012. She signed to Projekt Records the same year for the “Ice Iris” EP, followed by the album “Sugar Wingshiver” in 2014 and “Drawing up a Storm” in 2018. In 2019, recording as Polly Fae, she released the 15-track album “Dreamwalkers” on Projekt on 12 September, a limited-edition signed CD later followed by an instrumental version. The album “Phantom Gardens” followed the same year under the Paulina Cassidy name. Her Projekt output continued with “The Secret Language of Trees” and “Metamorphosis” in 2020, “Earthlight” in 2021 and “Glow” in 2022, alongside a “Dreamwalkers Instrumental” reissue. She contributed to the label’s “Purr24” various-artists compilation in 2024 and released the album “Ghostbirds” on 4 April 2025, followed later that year by a collaboration with Peter Phippen and Ivar Lunde Jr. on “The Phantom Moon.” “Lilac Cat” is her latest EP for Projekt Records, released 18 September 2026.
items._genre: ethereal dream pop / ambient pop / dream-jazz
items._cn_summary: 这篇内容本质上是Paulina Fae新EP《Lilac Cat》的发行新闻稿，而非原创乐评。文章详细列出了EP的发行信息、流媒体平台、曲目列表，以及唱片厂牌对作品的官方描述——将其定位为'ethereal dream pop'与'梦境般奇想'的集合，涵盖了从'galaxy-eyed whimsy'到'dream-jazz sounds'再到'faery-like currents'等元素。文中还回顾了Paulina Fae自2010年以来的完整音乐生涯，提及她在Projekt Records的长期合作关系，以及她作为视觉艺术家创作的塔罗牌和书籍作品。整篇文章缺乏对音乐本身的实质性评论、分析或个人见解，仅为信息汇编性质的发布通告，不包含任何关于声音设计、制作技巧、艺术价值或创作背景的深入探讨。作为dream pop/ethereal pop类型作品，与实验、前卫、爵士、电子等核心偏好的契合度有限。

items.body: Fairlight Children, the synthpop side project Apoptygma Berzerk’s Stephan L. Groth formed with Marianne B. and Tiff in the early 2000s, continues to surface in new contexts two decades after its debut album. The most recent example is the “V.A. 18. Elektrisch Festival Synth Pop Edition” 10″, released by Emmobiz Records on 27 February 2026, which carries an exclusive Fairlight Children bonus cut, “Before You Came Along (FC Edit),” alongside an equally exclusive Echo Image version, “Walk My Mind (Apop’s Short Walk Version).” Fairlight Children first appeared on record on 23 September 2003, contributing a version of “Bedsitter” to “A Tribute To Soft Cell: Non Stop Electro Cabaret.” That same year, Groth described the project at M’era Luna as heading toward retro synthpop, at a point when the next Apoptygma Berzerk album, “You And Me Against The World,” was moving in a rockier, guitar-driven direction. Fairlight Children gave him a separate outlet for the electro and 1980s synthpop material that record wasn’t going to hold, and the project’s name points to the same fascination: it references the Fairlight CMI, the digital sampling and synthesizer system that shaped 1980s studio production. The debut EP, “Before You Came Along,” followed on 2 February 2004, with a remix from Echo Image among its extras. The full-length “808 Bit” arrived on 15 March 2004 on Pitch Black Drive Productions, performed by Groth, Marianne B. and Tiff, with Iben Groth on vocals for the title track and Jon Erik Martinsen on Korg MS-20 for “Falling Out.” The Soft Cell tribute recording of “Bedsitter” found a home on the album as well. Contemporary coverage used Groth’s own description, “Electro Lounge,” for the record’s mix of melodic, playful electronics and open 1980s influences. 808 Bit by Fairlight Children The project then went quiet for more than fifteen years. A first signal of its return came in June 2020, when a Kevin Lux remix of “Invade My Heart Tonight” appeared on “Der Eisenberg Sampler Vol. 10.” On 24 July 2020, Pitch Black Drive Productions followed with the “CMI EP,” five reworkings of older Fairlight Children material: “808 Bit (Zone Tripper Remix),” “Invade My Heart Tonight (Alex O. Remix),” “Before You Came Along (Pleasure Remix),” “Falling Out (Monster Apparat Remix)” and a second “Before You Came Along (Panorama Remix).” Pleasure’s presence closed a loop of its own, having remixed “Falling Out” for the original 2004 EP and returning sixteen years later for the same track. The EP was mixed and mastered by Ole-Espen Kristiansen, with cover design by Alex O. Since then, Fairlight Children has stayed active only in scattered releases rather than as an ongoing project. Emmo.Biz Records issued “808 Bit” as a numbered, 400-copy picture disc with OBI in 2025, and the Side-Line archive previously covered that vinyl reissue in February 2025. The connection to Echo Image has also continued well past the 2004 remix: Echo Image returned in 2021 with the single “Walk My Mind” after 20 years of silence, including a remix by Apoptygma Berzerk, and by 2024 Groth was co-producing Echo Image’s comeback material directly, credited alongside Einar K. Five on the single “Madsong.” More than twenty years after Echo Image first remixed Fairlight Children, the “18. Elektrisch Festival Synth Pop Edition” 10″ puts both names on the same release again. About Fairlight Children Fairlight Children is a synthpop side project of Apoptygma Berzerk frontman Stephan L. Groth, formed with Marianne B. and Tiff after extensive touring behind the Apoptygma Berzerk album “Harmonizer.” Where the following Apoptygma Berzerk record, “You And Me Against The World,” pushed toward a rockier, guitar-oriented sound, Fairlight Children gave Groth a project built entirely around electronics, synthpop and the 1980s reference points behind its name, the Fairlight CMI sampling synthesizer. The project debuted on the compilation “A Tribute To Soft Cell: Non Stop Electro Cabaret” on 23 September 2003 with a cover of “Bedsitter,” followed by the “Before You Came Along” EP on 2 February 2004 and the album “808 Bit” on 15 March 2004, both released through Pitch Black Drive Productions, Groth’s own label. “808 Bit” featured Iben Groth on the title track’s vocals and Jon Erik Martinsen on Korg MS-20 for “Falling Out,” and drew a remix contribution from Echo Image. Fairlight Children was largely inactive between 2004 and 2020. A Kevin Lux remix of “Invade My Heart Tonight” on “Der Eisenberg Sampler Vol. 10” in June 2020 preceded the “CMI EP,” released by Pitch Black Drive Productions on 24 July 2020 with five remixes of earlier tracks by Zone Tripper, Alex O., Pleasure, Monster Apparat and Panorama, mixed and mastered by Ole-Espen Kristiansen. Emmo.Biz Records reissued “808 Bit” as a limited, numbered picture disc with OBI in 2025. Fairlight Children’s most recent appearance is an exclusive edit, “Before You Came Along (FC Edit),” on the “V.A. 18. Elektrisch Festival Synth Pop Edition” 10″, released by Emmobiz Records on 27 February 2026 alongside new and exclusive material from Solitary Experiments, Second Decay, Blind Passenger, KY, Chinese Detectives and Echo Image.
items._cn_summary: 本文以编年史方式回顾Fairlight Children这一合成器流行分支项目的完整历程，从2003年首张致敬录音到2026年最新合辑收录的独家混音版本。项目由Apoptygma Berzerk核心成员Stephan Groth与Marianne B.、Tiff共同创立，旨在探索纯电子与八十年代合成器流行风格。文章详细列出了每张EP和专辑的发行日期、厂牌、混音师及曲目信息，包括与Echo Image等关联项目的合作脉络。文中引用Groth本人提出的"Electro Lounge"定位，描述其作品融合旋律化电子与开放式的八十年代影响。整体内容偏向新闻性质的资料整理而非深入的音乐分析，涉及与暗潮/EBM领域有一定关联但本文呈现的更多是主流合成器流行脉络下的怀旧复古风格。

items.body: Ministry released its eleventh studio album, “The Last Sucker”, on 18 September 2007 through 13th Planet Records. The album turns 19 this year. MusicBrainz lists a first-release date of 8 September 2007, while Wikipedia and Discogs both confirm 18 September 2007 for the US release; Side-Line marks the anniversary on the date corroborated by the two independent sources. Al Jourgensen and Dave Donnelly produced the album, recorded in May 2007 at 13th Planet Studios in El Paso, Texas, with John Bilberry engineering and Donnelly also handling mastering. “The Last Sucker” closed the trilogy of anti-George W. Bush albums that began with “Houses of the Molé” (2004) and continued with “Rio Grande Blood” (2006). Jourgensen told Billboard at the time that he intended it to be Ministry’s final album, joking he would rather “leave on top of my game” than keep recording into old age; the band did not release another studio album of new material until “Relapse” in 2012. What is on Ministry’s ‘The Last Sucker’ The album runs 11 tracks: “Let’s Go”, “Watch Yourself”, “Life Is Good”, “The Dick Song”, “The Last Sucker”, “No Glory”, “Death & Destruction”, “Roadhouse Blues” (a cover of The Doors), “Die in a Crash”, “End of Days (Pt. 1)” and “End of Days (Pt. 2)”, with a total running time of 55:58. Deluxe and promotional editions added remixes of “Watch Yourself”, “The Last Sucker”, “Die in a Crash”, “No Glory” and “Death & Destruction” as bonus tracks. Fear Factory frontman Burton C. Bell provided guest lead vocals on “Die in a Crash” and both parts of “End of Days”. Paul Raven, formerly of Killing Joke, played bass and guitar and contributed backing vocals on several tracks; Prong and Danzig guitarist Tommy Victor played guitars and bass throughout. Sin Quirin and keyboardist John Bechdel also performed on the album. Closing track “End of Days (Pt. 2)” samples Dwight D. Eisenhower’s 1961 farewell address on the military-industrial complex alongside a reprise of “O Fortuna”, which had opened “Houses of the Molé” at the start of the trilogy. About Ministry Ministry formed in Chicago in 1981, led by vocalist, multi-instrumentalist and producer Al Jourgensen, the band’s sole constant member. The debut album, “With Sympathy”, released through Arista in 1983 in a synth-pop style Jourgensen later disowned, was followed by a move toward industrial rock on Sire/Warner Bros. releases including “Twitch” (1986), “The Land of Rape and Honey” (1988) and “The Mind Is a Terrible Thing to Taste” (1989). “Psalm 69: The Way to Succeed and the Way to Suck Eggs” (1992) became the band’s commercial peak, reaching number 27 on the Billboard 200 and going platinum on the strength of “Jesus Built My Hotrod” and “N.W.O.”. After “Filth Pig” (1996) and “Dark Side of the Spoon” (1999), Ministry signed to Sanctuary and released “Animositisomina” (2003) before launching its own label, 13th Planet Records, with “Houses of the Molé” (2004), the first instalment of the anti-Bush trilogy that continued with “Rio Grande Blood” (2006) and closed with “The Last Sucker” (2007). Bassist Paul Raven died in October 2007, shortly after the album’s release. Jourgensen revived Ministry for “Relapse” (2012) and Ministry’s ‘From Beer to Eternity’ turns 13 on 6 September (2013), the latter completed following guitarist Mike Scaccia’s death during recording. Ministry has continued releasing albums on Nuclear Blast, including “AmeriKKKant” (2018), “Moral Hygiene” (2021) and “Hopiumforthemasses” (2024).
items._cn_summary: 本文是关于Ministry 2007年专辑《The Last Sucker》发行19周年的纪念性资讯文章，并非原创乐评。文章详尽罗列了专辑的制作信息、曲目列表、客串乐手（Fear Factory主唱Burton C. Bell、Killing Joke前成员Paul Raven、Prong/Danzig吉他手Tommy Victor）以及发行细节。该专辑是反布什三部曲的终章，前两部分别为《Houses of the Molé》与《Rio Grande Blood》，结尾曲采样了艾森豪威尔1961年告别演说并呼应了首张的开篇'O Fortuna'。文章还概述了乐队自1981年成立以来的风格演变，从早期合成器流行转向工业摇滚。作为工业摇滚代表作，Ministry的声音契合暗潮/EBM品味的边缘地带，但本文仅为资讯整合，缺乏对音乐本身的艺术性分析与评价。

ニューヨークのクラシック音楽エージェント、エンタテインメント会社勤務を経て、クラシック音楽を中心としたパフォーミング・アーツ全般について執筆、日本の戯曲の英訳も手掛け... 詳しく見る 音楽の友 編集部 月刊誌 1941年12月創刊。音楽之友社の看板雑誌「音楽の友」を毎月刊行しています。“音楽の深層を知り、音楽家の本音を聞く”がモットー。今月号のコンテンツはこちらバックナンバ... 詳しく見る ウクライナ・フリーダム・オーケストラが8月25日と26日、リンカーン・センターのデイヴィッド・ゲフェン・ホールで演奏会を行った。同団は、ウクライナ国内のオーケストラ所属メンバーやウクライナ国外に逃れた音楽家らをメンバーとして、ロシアのウクライナ侵攻に対する反応として、2022年にウクライナ系カナダ人指揮者、ケリー＝リン・ウィルソンによって結成された。 以来、ウクライナの文化とレジリエンスを世界に示し、犠牲者を追悼するとともに平和を訴えることを目的とするという同団は、夏のオフシーズンを中心に活動を続けている。いまだに停戦の明確な兆しは見出されないなか、この8月に行われた欧米ツアーには、「2026年インヴィンシブル（無敵）・ツアー」と、かなり直接的な名称が与えられている。 設立当初から同団には広報から芸術面までメトロポリタン歌劇場（MET）が深くかかわっており、METは昨シーズンの公演プログラム冊子にも、毎回ウクライナ支持のメッセージを掲載した。ポーランド国立歌劇場やウクライナ文化省も協力し、2023年以来、ウクライナ大統領夫人オレナ・ゼレンスカの後援を得ているという。 そのような背景を意識せずとも、民族的なつながりが感じられるメンバーの顔、演奏が終わったあとに抱き合ってお互いを讃えあう姿などに、このアンサンブルの成り立ちが特殊であり、特別であることが感じられる。 はたしてウィルソン率いる同団の演奏は、一糸乱れぬアンサンブルというわけではないものの、全体として柔軟なつながりで聴かせる魅力的なものだった。 ウィルソンはニューヨーク・フィルハーモニックからNHK交響楽団まで、すでにさまざまなオーケストラとシンフォニー指揮者としての経験を積んでいるが、少なくともニューヨークでは、これまでオペラ指揮者としての印象のほうが強かったように思う。 しかし25日に演奏されたベートーヴェン「交響曲第7番」では、同曲のような人気交響曲でも豊かな音色を聴かせるダイナミックな統率力が印象的だった。最終楽章は現代の演奏らしく猛烈に速いテンポだが、疾走感が持続して息切れするところがなく、爽快だ。 もっとも8月25日の最大の呼び物は、休憩前に演奏されたリーゼ・ダーヴィドセンがソリストのR.シュトラウス《4つの最後の歌》であった。今回のツアーはヨーロッパ5都市とニューヨークを回るものだったが、ヨーロッパ5都市ではダーヴィドセンは登場せず、曲も別のものとなっている。彼女の登場が実現したのは、彼女とMETのつながりが深いことに加え、9月のシーズン初日にヴェルディ《マクベス》でマクベス夫人を歌うため、たまたまニューヨークに滞在していたためと思われる。 ダーヴィドセンの歌は、言葉一つひとつのニュアンスを枝葉末節にこだわって抽出するより、真正面からたゆたうように聴かせる。その現代随一の声の力があってこその表現であり、年齢を重ねることによる解釈の深まりを予感させる余裕も感じさせてくれた。ウィルソンの指揮も、そんなダーヴィドセンの現在の美点を支える推進力のあるものだった。 ウクライナ・フリーダム・オーケストラのヴェルディ「レクイエム」から（8月26日、デイヴィッド・ゲフェン・ホール）© Richard Termine / Met Opera 8月26日にはヴェルディ「レクイエム」が演奏された。ここでは何よりも、METの合唱団メンバーによって構成されたMETコーラス・アーティスツの好演が印象的で、冒頭から最後まで緊張感を保ちながらも柔らかに深く響いた合唱は、この日最大の立役者であった。 METの中堅的存在であるアイリーン・ペレス（S）とソロマン・ハワード（Bs）に加え、ナタリー・ルイス（Ms）、ルネ・バルベラ（T）らソリストの歌唱も安定感のあるもので、とりわけペレスの声と歌唱は、現在のMETの水準を表すものとして興味深いものだった。 ウィルソンの指揮も、よく指摘されるこの曲のオペラ的なダイナミックさを抽出したものだった。そしてそのダイナミックさは、現代の戦争に対する恐怖と怒りにふさわしく感じられるもので、全体を鎮魂曲としてインスパイアされるものにしていた。 ちなみに両日とも冒頭にはウクライナ人作曲家の作品が演奏され、25日はマクシム・コロミレツ（1981年生まれ）の《The Mothers of Kherson》（ヘルソンの母たち）からの組曲が、26日にはボフダナ・フロリャク（1968年生まれ）の《グローリア》が演奏された。そしてアンコールとして最後には、弦楽曲として編曲されたウクライナ国歌が美しく演奏された。
items._cn_summary: 乌克兰自由管弦乐团在林肯中心举办两场公演，曲目涵盖贝多芬《第七交响曲》、理查·施特劳斯《最后四首歌》以及威尔第《安魂曲》。乐团由乌克兰本土及流亡音乐家组成，由加拿大籍乌克兰裔指挥凯莉-林·威尔逊执棒，旨在以音乐方式呼吁和平。评论聚焦于指挥对乐团的灵活统御、女高音达维森从容而有力量的诠释，以及大都会歌剧院合唱团的浑厚表现。两场演出均以乌克兰当代作曲家作品开场，并以改编版乌克兰国歌作为返场。整体演出带有强烈的政治与文化象征意味，但音乐本体仍以传统古典曲目为主，缺乏实验性或跨界融合元素。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — When your album is from 1970 and you manage to sound more stoned than your contemporaries, you're ahead in at least one area. This debut from DANDO SHAFT, while not actually a concert album in spite of the implications of its title, possesses a live feel that vacillates both shakily and tightly in at the intersection of JETHRO TULL, MOODY BLUES, JAN DUKES DE GREY, MUSHROOM, with a wink or two to FUCHSIA (which they do nonetheless predate) and LINDISFARNE. In all, this is, while not quite a missing link, a varied and more than competent collection with a few surprises to maintain freshness after so many decades, achieved through the harmony vocals, Celtic flourishes and just enough psych to keep the folk-weary from unhinging a jaw. To get a flavor for the best on offer here from the integrated styles, go for the EMTIDI-like "September Wine", the reflective ballad "In the Country", and the twangy and uplifting "End of the Game". Don't dismiss the later bonus tracks either if you can connect with then, but most of all, give this one a p.m with whatever comfort consumable you've been saving.
items._genre: prog folk / psych folk / british folk
items._cn_summary: Dando Shaft的首张专辑虽非真正的现场录音，却营造出松散而紧凑交错的现场质感。作品融合Jethro Tull式的民谣摇滚骨架与Moody Blues的精致感，辅以凯尔特装饰与轻量迷幻色彩，和声演唱是贯穿全作的亮点。整体编排注重器乐纹理的变化，民谣旋律线在电吉他与提琴的衬托下展开，段落之间留有即兴呼吸感。评论特别提及三首代表作：带有德国Krautrock气质的"September Wine"、内省的抒情曲"In the Country"以及明亮吉他拨奏驱动的"End of the Game"。作为一支英国六七十年代之交的民谣乐队，作品在传统民谣基底上加入了时代性的迷幻扩展，但整体仍属根植于英伦民谣传统的渐进民谣范畴，对追求实验性与前卫性的听众而言，冒险程度有限。

items.body: Review by RojerWilco — If you're a fan of early Kaipa, you'll enjoy this set. Has it really been 40 years? Roine and Michael are as excellent as you would expect, and Tomas and Ingemar have apparently picked up right where they left off 40 years ago, literally not missing a beat. To me, the surprise is Lalle Larsson. As with his work in Karmakanic, he makes everything he touches better.The track selection has been picked from Inget Nytt Under Solen (Nothing New Under the Sun) and Solo, with Det Tysta Guldet (The Silent Gold) coming from the Kaipa daCapo album. Unless you're actively cross referencing their music, you wouldn't notice the new track among the classic ones.Consider this the missing link in the Kaipa discography. It is an excellent addition to any Kaipa collection, and also makes a good entry point for those interested in early Kaipa.
items._genre: symphonic prog / classic prog / live album
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是瑞典乐队Kaipa四十周年纪念现场录音，精选自《Inget Nytt Under Solen》和《Solo》两张专辑，加上一首来自《Kaipa daCapo》的新作。乐评指出新老成员配合默契，键盘手Lalle Larsson的加入为乐队带来显著提升，其演奏风格延续了他在Karmakanic中的特色。新曲目与经典作品无缝衔接，不进行交叉比对几乎无法辨别。该作被视为Kaipa唱片史中缺失的一环，既适合老乐迷收藏，也可作为接触早期Kaipa的入门作品。整体定位为正统的交响前卫摇滚复兴现场，并未涉及实验性或跨界元素，与用户偏好的实验前卫、爵士、电子等方向存在较大距离。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — An American band that has both an unusual back story as well as quite the unusual motivation. Veterans who are somehow collectively inspired to represent and express a blend of Spanish colonizer and Native American tradition, mythos, and spirit.1. "(Intro) The Coming Of The Spaniards" (3:54) Alan Parsons Project-like Western choir mixed into a musical pastiche that sounds like something from a Spanish "spaghetti western" like soundtrack. It's like throwing APP together with Novella-era RENAISSANCE. Powerful and most excellent! (9.667/10)2. "The Benefits Of Breathing Quietly" (5:56) excellent piano-based APP prog over which singers John Baker and Jake Livgren provide some excellent, appropriately bombastic vocals--entwined and mutually supportive. The music is excellent, the story in the lyrics powerful, the overall effect quite emotional. This is the kind of music and song that reaffirms the reason prog exists! And this Lisa LaRue: She is a FORCE! (9.333/10)3. "The Plains? Truth" (6:49) an instrumental symphonic rock soundscape that reminds me of the best of bands like Kansas, The Dregs, and modern day Prog Folk band SOLSTICE. Excellent programming and computer-generated violin--and sound engineering! Lisa: Maestra: you are nothing short of a genius! This is great prog! (14/15)4. "Quivira Bound" (5:33) this one feels more like old prog, old classic rock. Bombastic opening with piano-based lull for John and Jake's vocal presentation to begin in, we quickly find ourselves back in classic STYX/SOLSTICE/IONA/DAVE BAINBRIDGE/ALAN PARSONS PROJECT territory though, of course, you have to substitute male vocal tracks for most of the female ones--and EXCELLENT are the performances of both John and Jake. Though John Baker's choice of electric guitar tone is a little odd, it works well enough to take nothing away from Lisa's excellent music. (9/10)5. "Moving Forward" (6:51) an instrumental of exemplar weave of prog solos, violin, real and otherwise, keyboard play of the very highest caliber, interesting and very effective guitar sound and styling choices, and some rather stupendous programming of the drums and rhythm section. This could've been early FROST* or BIG BIG TRAIN or THE FLOWER KINGS or THE TANGENT or even Open Sky-era IONA. I call this song a prog lover's wet dream! (15/15)6. "The Turk/Follow The Wind" (5:58) despite the relatively "weak" realistic tone and talent of singer Jake Livgren's voice, the music behind this song is, again, of the highest quality and caliber. Wow! Great chord and melodic pathways drive the music of this band deep into the pleasure zones of my brain. (9.5/10)7. "Nothing Is Everything" (7:34) more sophisticated and virtuosic symphonic prog music that features, this time, a real, "live" violin (though the previous one--on "The Plains? Truth" sounded just as authentic). The song moves through several motifs, shifting in keys and tempos while maintaining the piano-based full-spectrum prog with violin palette until the fourth minute in which Lisa's gorgeous piano play is isolated with guest Joe Deninzen's violin for a spell before the rest of the prog instruments rejoin. The melody choices are so awesome: piano and violin going back and forth each with totally-engaging lines and dynamics. At the five minute mark we move into a heavier, more dynamic section with pounding piano chords, guitar power chords, and soloing electric guitar before we bridge into a Spanish guitar-led section beneath which Lisa has the drums programmed with some excellent tom-and-bass drum flourishes. And soon enough it is over! Nice! I never expected that one to be an instrumental the whole way through. (13.75/15)8. "Carved From The Sun" (8:03) another stupendous prog rock instrumental that takes the listener on an exciting journey of dynamic multi-stimuli, all encapsulated into an action-packed whirlwind of enjoyable romantic slightly-pastoral NeoProg. Great bass, drum pacing, and, of course, keyboard work. I'm coming to fully comprehend what total melodic genius Lisa is: Amazing! So easy and comforting while never sacrificing sophistication and active lines from all of her instruments in the weaves. John's wah-wah-ed distorted guitar in the third minute is quite fitting but Lisa's continuous display of melodic and harmonic genius never quits! So many endorphin/goosebump moments generated by melodies, chord progression surprises, as well as palette and textural shifts. I am simply in awe. This is not only great prog it is music that I can (and will be) listen(ing) to for a long time into the future. This is music that not only rivals but I think surpasses that of my other favorite 21st Century NeoProg/Prog Folk band/artist, Solstice. (15/15)9. "Kicking Rocks" (4:20) though another great instrumental rendering (with a Marc COHN "Walking in Memphis"-like piano approach). Active bass, steady drums, organ and synths, and intermittent electric guitar shredding all add their sounds over the lively piano foundation. There is a weird "no sound" solo section at the end of the second minute but Lisa's confident piano playing never wavers, continues to deliver some wonderfully engaging work (to which I feel like playing "air piano"). The synth-supported multiple guitar soloing that occurs in the fourth minute is cool, too, but I could listen to Lisa's piano playing all day long--especially with recurring support of bursts of near-djenty bass-&-guitar passages. (9.125/10)10. "Prelude To Anywhere/Weekend Conquistadors" (5:45) more of the same piano styling from "Kicking Rocks" over and within which synths, shredding violins and metal guitars, as well as periodic bass and drums help out. There's a lot of the TRANS SIBERIAN ORCHESTRA Christmas music feel to this sound palette. John and/or Jake join in during a solo piano lull around the three-minute mark, signifying the switch to the "Weekend Conquistadors" half of the song--a lament about modern man's use (and misuse) of the land that once supported herds of bison and Native American tribes. Weird "distant and fading" strummed electric guitar ending as a couple quotes from literature or legend as delivered as spoken word over the top. (8.875/10)11. "Still Breathing" (5:58) long introduction eventually pans out in the second minute into a hard-driving violin-topped prog instrumental passage. This is disrupted around the 2:30 mark to allow plodding piano notes and increasingly thickening rock palette to support more of Lisa's computer-generated violin. John's guitars begin to increase in layers, gradually revealing some solo ideas until another sudden stop at the end of the fifth minute signals a shift back into the hard-driving motif of the second minute, over which John's twangy guitar steps up to really solo before the song's final chord--which is followed by a neighing horse whose hooves can then be heard galloping off onto the Plains. Solid prog if not so "perfect" as some of the previous compositions. (9/10)Total time 66:41There are many who will bemoan so much of this music being computer generated and "cleaned" but the end result--great prog music--cannot (and should not) be denied. Keyboard specialist Lisa LaRue is expressing a level of genius that not many prog artists have ever achieved. An album that is definitely in the running for 2026's Album of the Year--and deservedly so!A/five stars; a masterpiece of wonderful progressive rock music that taps into the palettes and energy of both the NeoProg and Prog Folk realms of progressive rock music and represent the talents of a musical genius who is totally new to me: Native American Lisa LaRue. HIGHLY recommended!

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以交响前卫摇滚为核心框架，将西班牙殖民者与北美原住民的文化传统与神话意象融合为创作主题。乐队由退伍军人组成，键盘手Lisa LaRue担任核心作曲力量，编制以钢琴、合成器、小提琴和电吉他为主，搭配两男声主唱交替演绎。编曲厚重而程式化，大量借鉴Alan Parsons Project、Kansas、Styx等乐队的手法，弦乐编排与键盘铺陈层次分明，但整体呈现偏向七十至八十年代经典前卫摇滚的复古审美。前原住民主题为概念注入了一定文化深度，但音乐语言本身并未突破传统前卫摇滚的框架，创新性有限。

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — 1973 was a banner year for Italian progressive rock. Alongside the universally acclaimed masterpieces that the genre's "four tenors" were producing at the same time (Io Sono Natto Libero, Felona E Sorona, Photos Of Ghosts, Arbeit Macht Frei), other classics emerged that left a lasting mark on the genre, even though most of them were short-lived. Aside from often contrived?or even trivial?reunions, bands like Cervello, Campo Di Marte, Festa Mobile, Blocco Mentale, Museo Rosenbach, L'Uovo Di Colombo, Semiramis as one-album "meteor" bands, with their sole album released in 1973?even though the last two groups mentioned have recently reemerged with a noteworthy album (and it's impossible to overlook Apoteosi's seminal album, which falls into the same category, though it was released in 1975). One might be tempted to place Alphataurus in the same golden category, with its superb self-titled debut album?provided one disregards its second album, recorded the same year but released only in 1992 following the dissolution of its creator, as well as *AttosecondO*, the 2012 release, which is excellent but not as indispensable as its illustrious predecessor.More than 50 years after that annus mirabilis, Alphataurus is back, led by two founding members, keyboardist Pietro Pellegrini and guitarist Guido Wassermann (who sadly passed away after the recording was completed). A second keyboardist, Andrea Guizzetti, who already appeared on AttosecondO strengthens the lineup, rounded out by the inevitable fresh blood: Tony Alemanno (a defector from the new The Trip) on bass, Diego Mariani on drums, and Franco Giaffreda on vocals, acoustic guitar, and flute?the latter having already made a name for himself about fifteen years ago as a member of Biglietto Per L'Inferno. Is this new Alphataurus reunion a pleasant surprise, much like S�miramis's was a few months ago?Yes, but only partly, because "2084: Viaggio nel Nulla", a dystopian fiction with philosophical and existential themes, alternates between RPI tracks that still have that special spark (a good half of the album) and a sort of classy but generic prog that seems to meander nonchalantly over bluesy chords ("Pista 6," oddly placed at the beginning of the album, is saved by a magical Mellotron bridge), unfortunately verging on high-end Italian rock-pop ("Viaggio nel Nulla," disappointing despite a promising start and a catchy melodic theme), much like PFM has done recently in its least inspired moments (in fact, singer Franco Giaffreda's voice can be compared to that of Franz Di Cioccio). "Flashback (apocalisse)" is more convincing with its clearly syncopated, off-beat rhythm reminiscent of Gentle Giant, its unapologetic melodic breaks, its playful little Moog solo, its jazzy nods, and its infectious positive energy. "Meta e met�" (6:36) packs a punch in the same league?or even a notch above?with unpredictable, rhythmic footwork, powerful solo uppercuts, and a melody as strong as steel set against a velvety backdrop. The album closes tenderly with "E=mc2," featuring a smooth melody and emphatic, slightly saccharine harmonies that boldly combine acoustic guitar and chamber orchestra?though it lacks that distinctive tension that is the hallmark of the best prog.None of this is disgraceful?in fact, it's quite pleasant?conscientiously crafted with today's resources in a highly professional manner by true prog enthusiasts. But the album as a whole struggles to inspire overwhelming enthusiasm and will likely fall short of satisfying the most demanding among us, eliciting little more than a polite and benevolent listen. This assessment may seem harsh, even unfair, but it must be acknowledged that we're a long way from the success of S�miramis's earth-shattering comeback.Except that it's not quite that simple, because *2084: Viaggio nel Nulla* contains an epic track that's sure to make you forget everything else: "Wormhole" (10:15) is exactly what you'd expect from such a legendary band. A dynamic first section, full steam ahead, that owes a great deal to Banco's heyday with its Hammond organ arpeggios and repetitive piano; a second, more acoustic section, structured like PFM's "Impressioni di Settembre," with a sublime chorus?a true challenge to anyone who tries to resist singing along at the top of their lungs?everything is designed to set off fireworks in our ears, dazzle us, and make the twinkling of the stars fade into the background. A well-crafted modern RPI album that you can happily listen to again and again, whistling the melodies as if you'd always known them, *2084: Viaggio nel Nulla* becomes, with "Wormhole," a must-hear release from an RPI veteran worthy of his legendary status.

items._cn_summary: Alphataurus乐队在沉寂五十余年后携新专辑回归，延续了意大利前卫摇滚的传统血脉。专辑以反乌托邦科幻叙事为框架，探讨哲学与存在主义主题，由键盘手Pellegrini和已故吉他手Wassermann领衔制作。专辑呈现两极化特征：一半曲目保留了RPI特有的火花——切分节拍、Moog独奏、爵士化转折与Mellotron段落令人回味；另一半则滑向意大利摇滚流行化的套路，蓝调进行曲式冗长铺陈，旋律虽流畅却缺乏锐度。人声被比作PFM的Franz Di Cioccio，部分段落接近高水准的摇滚流行制作。作为1973年那一批单张专辑乐队的迟来续章，制作精良但革新性有限，更像是对黄金年代的致敬而非开拓。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — As long as the Electric Light Orchestra maintained the premise of being a progressive rock band featuring strings, they could rely on those very strings, along with the right arrangements, to remain at the cutting edge. However, with each successive album following Roy Wood's departure, pop music began to take up more space in their compositions. "Fire on High" boasts a sweeping, powerful start, moving beyond the intro and the female chorus to showcase that signature element established in their first three albums: a classical-rock orchestra. Yet, while the compositions on those early records were daring and surprising, featuring dark, original arrangements that coexisted with rock 'n' roll, the music gradually became more predictable. Face the Music is an enjoyable listen, though it has its ups and downs; "Waterfall," for instance, is a ballad that, were the strings stripped away, I could easily imagine Freddie Mercury singing. Those strings could be mysterious, aggressive, or melancholic, and at times even reminiscent of the Beatles, echoing the production style of George Martin."Evil Woman" is a great song, the first of the nods to disco they would incorporate, yet played in a glam-rock and funk style. It's a spirited, groovy track featuring prominent drums and Bee Gees-style backing vocals; the strings serve the disco vibe, complemented by a funky clavinet part that made, and still makes, the song a lot of fun (proving that progressive rock can be fun, too). At times, the strings would play around and break the conventional mold, and whenever Jeff Lynne was in a festive mood, he really brought a great vibe to the music."Nightrider" is built upon the backing vocals and all the signature trappings they had established, the voices and the swirling strings that seemed to spin like a Ferris wheel. Yet, it still sounded fresh; at times, the music would hang suspended in mid-air, leaving the female backing vocals alone for a few seconds before everything instantly rushed back in. There was also a dreamlike section, a compositional triumph, infused with a burst of energy that snapped the listener out of that reverie; it was in moments like these that ELO truly shone with a symphonic brilliance."Poker" was another fast-paced rock 'n' roll track, yet Richard Tandy's Minimoog, Lynne's guitar, and the cellos combined to create magnificent sonic moments; meanwhile, "Strange Magic", which begins like Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake, transforms into a radio-friendly mid-70s ballad. For some reason, the influence of the Bee Gees and Queen hovers over the album, intertwining with the electric originality of this orchestra. "Down Home Town" succumbs to an inexplicable country vibe, though the string arrangements are effectively tailored to that style. "One Summer Dream" begins with the gravity of an opera's finale, with melancholy taking the lead, yet it balances out a solid, worthy album that delivers all the virtues and strengths one would expect from the band. The choruses and those robust string parts the band could latch onto saved it from the electric chair, which they could simply walk right past.

items._cn_summary: 这张1975年专辑标志着电光乐团从激进前卫向流行领域倾斜的转折点。评论指出早期作品中那种大胆、暗黑且出人意料的编曲逐渐被可预测性取代，弦乐编排虽仍保持古典摇滚交响团的标志性特质，但整体趋向商业化与电台化。专辑尝试融入迪斯科、放克、乡村等多种风格，弦乐在神秘、激进与忧郁之间切换，试图打破常规模式。Track如"Evil Woman"以华丽摇滚和放克律动带来欢快感，"Nightrider"则在女声和声与旋转弦乐中展现梦幻气质，"Strange Magic"从天鹅湖式开场过渡为中速抒情。整体制作精良但创新性已不如前作，是一支从实验边缘稳步迈向主流市场的乐队在这个阶段留下的录音。

items._cn_summary: Zoe Rahman 为纪念2024年世界钢琴日，受赫尔爵士音乐节委约创作了钢琴组曲《Hull Suite》，最初设计为独奏形式，后加入贝斯与鼓的声部。此次在伦敦Vortex俱乐部演出时，与长期合作的低音提琴手Alec Dankworth和鼓手Gene Calderazoo组成三重奏呈现作品。作为英国爵士钢琴领域具有学院派背景的演奏家，Rahman的创作融合了当代爵士的即兴语汇与英国本土爵士场景的细腻表达，作品从独奏版本扩展至三重奏编制，展现了她在钢琴主导的现代爵士语言中的探索。该文章为乐评开头部分，正式评价内容未充分展示。整体而言属于当代爵士范畴，与听众关注的实验前卫领域存在一定距离。

items.body: French industrial project HORSKH has released “Connected“, a collaboration with Carpenter Brut, on September 10, 2026, ahead of HORSKH’s forthcoming album “MTNT”. HORSKH’s official Bandcamp credits the track jointly to HORSKH and Carpenter Brut, with mixing and mastering by Thibault Chaumont at Deviant Lab Studio and artwork by Johanna Jaskowska. Connected by HORSKH “Connected” also appears on HORSKH’s forthcoming album “MTNT”, listed as a ten-track release scheduled for September 25, 2026, issued through Wire Control under exclusive licence to Blood Blast Distribution. “Connected” and the earlier single “Glow” are both tied directly to “MTNT”. The lyrics give the collaboration a considerably less comfortable meaning than its title suggests. Images of wires, intravenous connection, fear, chemical illusion and an attachment that persists despite attempts to escape recur throughout the song, placing bodily, technological and psychological attachment close together rather than treating “connection” as straightforward communication. The pairing brings together two French projects that approach heavy electronic music from different but intersecting angles. HORSKH’s recent catalogue has increasingly combined guitars, electronic programming and industrial pressure: “BODY” arrived in January 2024, following “WIRE” in 2021 and “GATE” in 2017. Carpenter Brut, meanwhile, released his latest studio album “Leather Temple” on February 27, 2026. The two releases share a technical link as well: “Leather Temple” was mixed and mastered by Thibault Chaumont at Deviant Lab, the same studio and engineer credited on “Connected”. “MTNT” arrives on September 25, 2026. “Connected” is available now through HORSKH’s official Bandcamp and streaming platforms. About HORSKH HORSKH are based in Besançon, France. Their recorded catalogue dates back to the “DAWN” EP, released in October 2014 and followed by an expanded edition in 2015. Their first full-length album, “GATE”, arrived on April 10, 2017, followed by “WIRE” on January 22, 2021 and “BODY” on January 19, 2024. The credits for “GATE” and “WIRE” list Bastien on programming, keyboards, vocals and guitar, Briou on live drums, and Jordan on guitar and keyboards. “WIRE” was mixed by Sam Munnier and Bastien Hennaut and mastered at Deviant Lab Studio, while “BODY” was mixed and mastered by Thibault Chaumont at Deviant Lab Studio. Ahead of “MTNT”, HORSKH released three other singles during 2026: “BAD GLITCH” on January 22, “Hyperhuman” in March and “Glow” in June. “Connected”, featuring Carpenter Brut, followed on September 10. The band have also been active on the European festival circuit in 2026, with appearances listed at Wave-Gotik-Treffen in Leipzig, Castle Party in Bolków and Nocturnal Culture Night in Deutzen, alongside a series of French dates extending into November. The catalogue combines programmed electronics, guitars and live percussion across industrial, EBM and electro-adjacent territory, reflecting the band’s own album credits. About Carpenter Brut Carpenter Brut is the stage name of Franck Hueso, a French darksynth musician from Poitiers active since 2012. He released three EPs, “EP I” (2012), “EP II” (2013) and “EP III” (2015), later compiled as the album “Trilogy” (2015), followed by “Leather Teeth” (2018), the “Blood Machines” soundtrack (2020), “Leather Terror” (2022) and “Leather Temple” (2026). His releases since 2015 have come out through his own label, No Quarter Prod. In live performances, Carpenter Brut is joined by guitarist Adrien Grousset and drummer Florent Marcadet, both also members of the French metal band Hacride.
items._cn_summary: HORSKH 与 Carpenter Brut 合作的单曲'Connected'作为专辑'MTNT'的前置发布，混合了工业电子的压迫感与合成器驱动的律动。歌词围绕导线、静脉连接、化学幻觉与无法挣脱的依附等意象展开，将身体、技术与心理层面的'连接'并置，而非将其简单理解为沟通。HORSKH 近作以吉他、电子编程与工业张力结合为方向，Carpenter Brut 则延续其暗色合成器路线。两者在制作层面共享同一录音棚与混音师 Thibault Chaumont，技术关联紧密。内容为新闻信息发布式报道，侧重发行日期、厂牌与制作人员等事实罗列，缺乏对音乐本身声音质感或结构创新的深度评述。

items.album: Ray Noir releases ‘Gothstar’ EP with Danny Blu collaboration and new track ‘Crush’
items.excerpt: London-based queer alt-metal artist Ray Noir released “Gothstar” on September 17th 2026, a six-track EP that mixes metalcore guitars with rave and electronic club production. Ray Noir’s “Gothstar” EP is out digitally and on vinyl and CD. The EP collects the four singles issued since April 2026 and adds two new recordings. It opens with “Label Whxre” and continues with “Black”, “Boys”, and “Gothstar” featuring Danny Blu
items.body: London-based queer alt-metal artist Ray Noir released “Gothstar” on September 17th 2026, a six-track EP that mixes metalcore guitars with rave and electronic club production. Ray Noir’s “Gothstar” EP is out digitally and on vinyl and CD. The EP collects the four singles issued since April 2026 and adds two new recordings. It opens with “Label Whxre” and continues with “Black”, “Boys”, and “Gothstar” featuring Danny Blu, the New York artist and former Echo Black frontman. The new track “Crush” follows, and “Gothstar (Alternative Version)”, a solo version of the title track, closes the record. Ray Noir wrote the material with Jon Cass and Tom Saint, who are also the EP’s producers. The track credits for “Black” and “Crush” list Cass as producer and Saint for additional production, mixing and mastering, with Saint also singing backing vocals on “Crush”. Cass, a member of UK post-hardcore band As Everything Unfolds, previously produced Ray Noir’s 2025 EP “Against The Machine”. The release material describes the EP as dealing with identity, confidence and sexuality, with “Gothstar” as both a character and an attitude at its centre. Ray Noir commented: “Growing up in the Norwegian metal scene, I didn’t really see anyone like me. With Gothstar, I wanted to create the world I wish I’d had back then. It’s gay, it’s heavy, it’s sweaty, it’s camp and it doesn’t take itself too seriously. Basically, if Berghain had a mosh pit, I’d like to think this would be playing.” “Crush” is the focus track of the EP. Ray Noir based it on his own experience of growing up in Norway’s metal scene and on “Heated Rivalry”, Rachel Reid’s gay ice hockey romance novel, which was adapted for television in 2025. The lyrics name the story’s lead couple, Ilya and Shane, and include lines in Norwegian. Four singles ahead of the EP “Label Whxre” opened the “Gothstar” campaign on 2 April 2026. “Black” followed on 14 May 2026 with a video directed by Ray Noir, and “Boys” arrived in June 2026 with a video filmed at Slim Jim’s Liquor Store in Islington, north London. The title track “Gothstar” featuring Danny Blu came out on 13 August 2026 together with an official music video. ‘Gothstar'”‘ release party in London Ray Noir marks the release with a party at Slim Jim’s Liquor Store on Saturday 19 September 2026, the venue where the “Boys” video was filmed. Tom Saint is listed as special guest. Entry is free, with tickets via Ray Noir – Gothstar EP Release Party on DICE. Get the EP as vinyl or CD here! About Ray Noir Ray Noir is a queer alternative artist based in London. His official biography places his background in Oslo’s black-metal underground, and his sound combines metal guitars with electronic club production. He released his first single, “Double Trouble”, in 2014. In October 2023 he issued “Pity Party“, the lead single from the mixtape “Scorpio”, followed on 1 November 2023 by “Latency“. The seven-track “Scorpio” arrived in 2024, and his official biography lists a top-five placement in the German Alternative Charts. A deluxe edition of “Scorpio” followed in July 2024, adding “All Alone” featuring Mariann Rosa of Surferosa, a “Double Trouble” remix by TOVA, remixes by Gothminister, Corlyx and Tension Control, and “You, Me & The Devil” featuring Tom Saint. That August he supported Combichrist at the Underworld in London and played the Electro Night in Oslo at Revolver with Piston Damp on 31 August 2024. On 14 February 2025 he released “Razorblade Romance“, written with Steve Stevens and Madeleine Wood, featuring Stevens on guitar and produced and mixed by Jon Cass. A cover of Tears for Fears’ “Shout” followed in May 2025, with guitar by Arno Von Detritus and backing vocals by Ben Christo of The Sisters of Mercy. “Dead Valentine” came out on 3 July 2025 and announced the EP “Against The Machine”, released on 18 September 2025 with “Razorblade Romance”, “Dead Valentine”, “Mad World” and an alternative version of “YMATD”. A deluxe edition followed in December 2025 with remixes by Tension Control, Verona On Venus, Junkie Kut and Ays Kura, alongside vinyl and CD editions. Ray Noir opened 2026 with the singles “Temptation” in January and “Breathe” in February. “Gothstar” is his second EP after “Against The Machine” and continues his work with Jon Cass, who produced both EPs, and Tom Saint, who also featured on the 2024 “Scorpio” deluxe edition.

items.body: Town & Towers Records releases Eckotrigger‘s new single Imposter on Friday, September 18. The London and Copenhagen duo mixes synthpop, darkwave and alternative electronic songwriting on a track about confronting the past, emotional relapse and the search for inner peace. Eckotrigger describes “Imposter” as being “about trying to cut free from the past as we strive towards our own peace”. The song opens with the lines “I lay awake / In a sense of doom” before settling into a recurring refrain, “My emotional state / Takes me back to places”, that returns throughout the track to describe being pulled back into experiences the narrator believed had been left behind. The lyrics trace the process of letting go of people, memories and earlier versions of oneself, arriving at a closing message: “Nothing stays the same”. “Imposter” follows the release of Eckotrigger’s debut album “Reflections”, issued on CD and 12″ vinyl in late May 2026 and available through the band’s release page. The new single is not yet listed on the duo’s Bandcamp page; “Imposter” can currently be found through the Town & Towers Records aggregator link above, which routes to Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, Deezer, Tidal and SoundCloud. About Eckotrigger Eckotrigger is a duo formed in London, UK, comprising producer and instrumentalist Paul Dogra and vocalist and lyricist Joel Alexander. The pair, who now split their time between London and Copenhagen, built the project after playing in other bands and wanting to work without the friction of a full group, drawing on a shared appreciation for Depeche Mode, David Bowie, Nine Inch Nails, The Cure and The National. The duo released its debut single in December 2020 with an accompanying video addressing mental health and addiction, which received radio play and was discussed on BBC Radio. In September 2021, Eckotrigger performed in a 24-hour online concert for World Peace Day. The band signed to the Danish label Town & Towers Records in August 2022 and has since released several singles and an EP, including “Collide”, which appeared in its extended form on the conzoom Records compilation “electropop.25” in 2023. Joel Alexander has also lent vocals and lyrics outside the duo, featuring on Danish artist ee:man’s single “Slow Dream”, also released via Town & Towers Records. Eckotrigger played Elektroland Festival and Electrofest in Denmark in 2023, performed three UK concerts in 2024, supported Empathy Test, and played Emergenza Festival and the Live Wired event in Copenhagen in 2026. The band’s debut album, “Reflections”, followed on CD and 12″ vinyl in late May 2026. “Imposter” is the duo’s first single since that album.

items.body: Los Angeles club Das Bunker marks its 30th anniversary this October with three events: a Catch One show headlined by Combichrist on October 2, a Nine Inch Nails-themed boat cruise called Nine Inch Sails on October 10, and a Halloween dance party on October 31. Combichrist headlines Das Bunker’s 30th anniversary at Catch One Combichrist returns to Das Bunker for the first time since 2009 to headline the club’s official 30th anniversary show at Catch One on October 2. The set draws on the band’s first three albums, “The Joy of Gunz” (2003), “Everybody Hates You” (2005) and “What The Fuck Is Wrong With You People?” (2007). Richmond, Virginia’s The Treasury, whose sound mixes EBM, synth-punk, post-punk and 1990s techno, opens. Das Bunker resident DJs Mimi Cry, IHX, Franck H Bomb and The Operative play the rest of the 21+ night, which runs from 9pm to 3am. A Nine Inch Nails boat cruise and a Halloween party close out the month On October 10, Nine Inch Sails departs from Long Beach, California, the port city where Das Bunker started as a club. Das Bunker offshoot 90s Goth Klub and Depeche Boat present the 21+, three-hour, two-room cruise: DJ Bractune plays Nine Inch Nails on the outdoor deck while DJ Eser covers goth, darkwave and new wave on the second room. The anniversary month closes on October 31 with a Halloween party at Catch One, presented by 90s Goth Klub and Body Rhythm across two rooms of goth, darkwave and new wave. DJs J Bractune, Rev.John and Angel Tears play the 21+ event. About Das Bunker Das Bunker was founded in Long Beach, California on October 22, 1996, to spotlight industrial and related genres that other Los Angeles clubs overlooked before relocating its regular night to Catch One. Over three decades the club has hosted Front 242 and other established industrial and EBM acts alongside emerging names, and has run recurring nights including History of Industrial, Summer Massive and Das Bunker Star Wars Night. Its coverage has included the Los Angeles Times, Vice and Post Punk. Side-Line covered Das Bunker’s 29th anniversary last October, when Unter Null headlined at Catch One. This year’s 30th anniversary run adds Combichrist, a Nine Inch Nails cruise and a Halloween party to that annual tradition.

items.body: Aggrotech and dark electro project Subliminal Code released an official video for “Behind the Mask“, the title track from the single issued through Neon Retro Records on July 31, 2026. Side-Line covered the single’s five-track remix package when a People Theatre remix, an Elektroterapi remix, a club version and a Dominator remix were added on August 16; the video now gives the title track its own visual counterpart. The project describes its sound as combining “Industrial, Aggrotech, Dark Electro, EBM and Hard Techno”, and says “Behind the Mask” continues that direction with “a cinematic visual concept inspired by classic psychological horror and 80s slasher cinema.” Behind the Mask by Subliminal Code About Subliminal Code Subliminal Code was founded at the start of 2010 by Raul Jose Padron and Raul Junior Padron, drawing on EBM, industrial, metal and synthpop; the twin brothers trace their roots to Venezuela, with the project now based between Venezuela and Hungary. Side-Line has followed the project’s chronology from the “Malevolencia” single in 2020 through the “The Cancer Of The World Is Human Beings” album in 2021 and on to the “Behind the Mask” single and its remix package this year. “Behind the Mask” is the first Subliminal Code release to carry Neon Retro Records, and the new video is its first official visual.

items.body: At sundown, even a familiar landscape can begin to feel strange, its ordinary landmarks suggesting places you might once have visited in a dream. On Western, The Church gives that feeling an easy, unhurried shape. A shuffling drumbeat keeps moving with quiet resolve while gentle guitar chimes and a bed of breezy synths suggest the tall shadows cast by the last light spreading across the desert. Beneath them, the bass holds a deep, rounded groove, giving Steve Kilbey room to sing with the calm of someone who has already heard every objection. Recorded in Austin, Texas, Western offers another look at Lacuna, the Australian band’s 28th album, due October 30, 2026 via Cooking Vinyl. The 17-track record follows their recent singles-celebrating world tour, with this latest release picking up after Sacred Echoes Part II. Kilbey’s matter-of-fact yet nostalgic delivery gives the song its peculiar comfort. You could picture him singing from the corner of a dim saloon, entertaining a few gamblers with a story whose details become stranger with each telling. His voice carries a trace of resignation and a dry amusement, taking each improbable turn in stride. Around him, the guitars leave space for the rhythm to breathe, their wistful and twangy post-punk melodies carrying a dusky bittersweetness that seems perfectly at ease with itself. The lyrics seem to wander from men rolling dice to strange encounters, glimpses of another world, and eventually outer space. Those abrupt changes of scene suit the music’s steady momentum, with Kilbey following each detour as casually as he might describe the route home. Across three minutes, Western makes a rambling, faintly dangerous adventure feel as easy as watching the sun go down. “Well, we were in Texas, weren’t we?” laughs Kilbey. “As a kid, all there was on TV were Westerns, so I let it all soak in and this is what came out. Some nice six-string bass counter riffs going, and the song is basically a shaggy dog story that just jumps all over the place… breezy and uncomplicated.” Listen to Western below: Formed in 1980, The Church have spent 46 years exploring the meeting points of post-punk, psychedelia, and dream pop, with songs including The Unguarded Moment, Almost With You, Under the Milky Way, and Reptile marking different stages of that history. Their current six-piece lineup brings Kilbey together with longtime drummer and producer Tim Powles, guitarists Ian Haug and Ashley Naylor, multi-instrumentalist Jeffrey Cain, and newest member, drummer Nicholas Meredith. Lacuna is out October 30, 2026, through Cooking Vinyl. Pre-order the album here. Lacuna tracklist: Lumbini Grove Western Ferrari Sky River Winter Have You Been Here Before The Lemurian Everytime Sky and Hill Paladin Martian Skyline I Want It The Place of Eternal Spring Rapture Forever Lumbini Theme (Slight Return) Sacred Echoes Follow The Church: Website Instagram Facebook The post The Church Rides Again With Their Latest Single “Western” — New Album “Lacuna” Announced! appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: The Church 即将发行第28张专辑《Lacuna》，首支单曲《Western》在德州奥斯汀录制，延续乐队一贯的梦幻流行与后朋克融合风格。歌曲以慵懒的鼓点和清脆的吉他音调营造出黄昏沙漠的氛围，合成器层铺陈出宽广的声场，贝斯线条沉稳圆润。Steve Kilbey 的演唱平静而略带怀旧，歌词从掷骰子的男人漫游到外太空，场景跳跃自如。吉他旋律带有忧郁的乡村色彩，在后朋克的骨架上增添了一丝苍凉与超现实感。整首歌三分钟内的叙事如同一段散漫的冒险故事，氛围松散却自洽。这是一支旋律悦耳但缺乏实验野心的成熟乐队作品，主要面向资深后朋克与梦幻流行乐迷。

東京藝術大学、ミラノ·ヴェルディ音楽院、チューリッヒ音楽大学大学院、スイス国立オペラスタジオを経て、スイス連邦認定オペラ歌手となるが、声域の変更に伴い廃業。環境ビジネ... 詳しく見る 音楽の友 編集部 月刊誌 1941年12月創刊。音楽之友社の看板雑誌「音楽の友」を毎月刊行しています。“音楽の深層を知り、音楽家の本音を聞く”がモットー。今月号のコンテンツはこちらバックナンバ... 詳しく見る ルツェルン音楽祭が、セバスティアン・ノルドマン新総裁の企画である「序曲」と題した無料公演で、8月13日に開幕した。公開リハーサルの様相で、リッカルド・シャイー以下ルツェルン祝祭管弦楽団の楽団員は普段着だったが、それがまた親近感を抱かせる。 プログラムも、スティーヴ・ライヒ《ニューヨーク・カウンターポイント》のあとはガーシュウィン《キューバ序曲》、バーンスタイン《ウェスト・サイド・ストーリー》から〈マンボ〉と楽しめるプログラムだったのは、今年のテーマが「アメリカン・ドリーム」だからだ。シャイーはこのところ、これらのレパートリーを各地で披露しているといい、彼の新たな顔が見られる。 続いて会場のルツェルン・カルチャー・コングレスセンター（KKL）前に設置された野外ステージで、ハバナ・リセウム・オーケストラとベルリン・フィルハーモニー管弦楽団のホルン奏者、サラ・ウィリスがラテン調のモーツァルトや《カルメン》等、キューバ音楽を奏で、踊り出す聴衆も多くいて、熱いオープニングとなった。 15日は今年のアーティスト・エトワール、アウグスティン・ハーデリヒが登場、クラウス・マケラ指揮の祝祭管とバーバー「ヴァイオリン協奏曲」を研ぎ澄まされた音で奏で、まるでおとぎ話の世界のような共演だった。 2年前にアメリカの永住権も取ったというハーデリヒが愛情を込めて紡ぎ出す音に、マケラが応える様子が室内楽のように精緻だ。アンコールもアーヴィン・T・ラウズ《オレンジ・ブロッサム・スペシャル》で、アメリカンな選曲だった。 後半はストラヴィンスキー《火の鳥》を熱演し、マケラは何度も聴衆に呼び戻された。 8月17日はダニエル・バレンボイムが指揮するウェスト=イースタン・ディヴァン管弦楽団が、ヨーヨー・マとドヴォルジャーク「チェロ協奏曲」で匠の共演を聴かせた。後半はシューマン「交響曲第3番《ライン》」で若々しさも見せた。 8月23日にはコンポーザー・セミナーが6人の若手作曲家に委嘱した作品を、6曲一斉に世界初演した。このセミナーはピエール・ブーレーズが始めた現代曲アカデミーを基礎に、2016年にヴォルフガング・リームが立ち上げたもので、今年は4人の若手指揮者も招かれた。 作曲家同席の下、今年も110人が参加するルツェルン祝祭現代管弦楽団と創り上げた音が、歓びに満ちて生まれ出た。今年は日本人の参加者も多く、ヴァイオリンの伊勢宥奈、ヴィオラの布施海里、チェロの蕨野真美、フルートの矢島雄太郎、テューバの山本蒼太、ピアノの船橋佑花らが生き生きと演奏。日本の音楽界を支えていく次世代が、世界の現代音楽の第一線を学ぶ姿に頼もしさを感じた。 チェチーリア・バルトリの、涙を誘う《オルフェオとエウリディーチェ》 観客の拍手に応えるチェチーリア・バルトリ。今年還暦（60歳）を迎えた© Peter Fischli / Lucerne Festival 夜には当音楽祭の人気者、チェチーリア・バルトリがグルック《オルフェオとエウリディーチェ》で聴衆を喜ばせた。このプロダクションは、ザルツブルクからウィーンを回り、以前はチューリヒ・トーンハレでも見たが、その時よりも音楽的により深くなっていた。 暗くなった舞台にエウリディーチェ役のメリッサ・プティ（アモーレ役も兼任）が横たわり、蝋燭のような灯りを持ったモンテカルロ歌劇場合唱団が登場するだけで舞台装置ができあがる。そして彼らの歌により情景が描かれるため、字幕は必須、とバルトリは語る。 今年還暦を迎えた彼女はKKLを満たすほどの声量はないが、代わりに弱声はどんどん研ぎ澄まされ、涙を誘う。それに、ジャンルカ・カプアーノが指揮するピリオド楽器オーケストラ「モナコ公の音楽家たち」がそっと寄り添う。今回は歌詞を歌わずに叫ぶような部分も複数見られ、魂の震えを歌っていると実感させた。 有名なオルフェオのアリア〈エウリディーチェを失って〉は、いつもバルトリは超速で歌うのが残念なのだが、今回は繰り返し部分でしっとりと絶望感を表現したため、ここでも涙が込み上げる。 終演後、楽屋へ行くと、バルトリの御母堂も涙を溜めており、バルトリも「ほんとうに良い音楽」といって、まるでオルフェオとエウリディーチェの葬送に参列した人のようだった。この音楽的共感力が好演の理由だろう。

items.body: Lost Tribe Sound will be releasing three albums from William Ryan Fritch this summer. A History, in Boxes is a uniting between Fritch and writer and spoken word artist Matt Finney. The other two, an extended edition of The Old Believers and The Sum of its Parts, both come from his vault of music for film… A History, In Boxes is the sound of growing up, the sound of stepping onto the porch and arriving home after baseball practice. Youthful rites and rituals still burn in the heart: those endless, deep-pan summers still glint against the horizon, as do those first dates and the unashamed selfies that were taken as the sunset glowed against her face. Loving and losing both your teenage sweetheart and your virginity in encountering suffering for the first time is one part of the passage: the deep trauma of heartbreak is one of a thousand experiences that, while bittersweet, are there for a reason: they make you feel alive. Finney’s spoken word is from the heart, leaking with a delaying smile and a tear at the cusp of the eye, but it’s always full of appreciation and gratitude. This is a sweeping slice of Americana, a long-lost relation of a new, explosive folk with a soft inner centre (thanks to the banjo), with electro-acoustic elements similar in vein to post-post-rock. Wise and weary words say the things that’ve settled in the heart. Secret emotions come alive in these vocal love-letters, painting in cherry lipstick Finney’s sublime use of words. Sliding melodies and sun-drained strings swirl in the atmosphere, their light eclipsed by tall trees and summers gone. Propulsive drums energize the music, and they don’t want to give up the feeling – they cling to it. The drumming is elephantine in size and is also a primal war cry, a desperate appeal to anyone who’ll listen during the depths of heartbreak, while ‘Courthouse Wedding’ is a teenage dream, pre-drama, its bleached boards and high windows sunbathing in summer light. This album is about two women who changed my life. I loved them and lost them both. I was young and stupid and not ready for either of them but they taught me a lot. – Finney In 2014, only three years ago, William Ryan Fritch and Lost Tribe Sound began releasing a series of twelve albums over a two-year stretch. The Old Believers was a part of that gigantic Leave Me Series. Musically, The Old Believers has a very different tone. Its classical leaning automatically brings about a darker atmosphere. As well as bringing back the original score, the music has been rearranged and the album features eight new and reworked compositions. Music was used from two other recent films highlighting the harrowing situations of those displaced and seeking safe refuge, one of them being the 2016 academy award nominated documentary ‘4.1 Miles’. But calling the music a ‘score’ is a bit of an injustice. While it would be classified (urggggg) as soundtrack music, it’s so much more than that. Why should it prop up a scene on the screen when it has a life of its own? Soundtracks are usually staccato-stilted collections, but this is cohesive and broad in scope. Fritch’s compositions are jaw-dropping behemoths. His skills in this area are well-documented. Sure, we’ve known about them for a while, but that doesn’t diminish the power of the music. One segment emerges as a shy and softly-spoken soul, a delicately plucked instrumental, while the next explodes with volcanic force. The music has a common, brooding theme at its core, a tension that never settles or stabilizes; no resolutions, mirroring the horrors of uncertainty and the ill anxieties of a life without security or shelter. The strings don’t bend willingly towards a sense of peace. There are tender moments within, and their brevity makes it all the more moving. You can find temporary refuge in its crumbling stone walls and its ancient abbeys, and the album is long enough to find a secluded place within its music. ‘Who Fell the Last Tree’ adds to a sober sky, and its liberated percussion puts a thoughtful, mature musicianship in the limelight. There’s something of native tradition inside the music, of aged folk music and old ways. The dusty strings are caught up in an uneasy alliance with the present, a swirling integration that somehow works, but these old traditions give the music a feeling of warmth in spite of its overcast weather, and the music is kept safe from harm. The Sum of its Parts starts off in equally dark territory, thanks in part to its classical manifestations, its hanging notes and its low-registered appearances. You should never judge someone based on their appearance, though, and the same is true in music…if you look closer – deeper – you’ll find that the music is livelier than the leaden, conservative-leaning The Old Believers. The music’s got the blues, staring down into an empty bottle at two in the morning, but the second track seems to contradict this as strings wake up and smell the coffee. Come the morning, there’s no risk of a hangover. The swelling sun lights up the space in an orange and amber light, the glowing dawn promising something special for the day ahead. The music has a stronger aftertaste than coffee; when it begins to pump, getting into its proper gear, it carries something like the clanking of cogs in an iron machine, its smell like that of a copper coin or the frizzling air seconds before a lightning strike. The recurring motifs – a staple in film scoring – are strong enough to not need an accompanying image. The mood isn’t exactly oppressive, but its classical approach ages the music and wrinkles its skin…its bones appear as worn-down sets of ivory, but its spirit is spritely. The music gracefully transfers from a thoughtful mood to an energetic release, swooning into the unknown. Sometimes this happens in a single piece, as on ‘Subconsciously’, but others spread themselves out. So many artists overthink things…and their music asphyxiates because of it, burdened by unnecessary baggage and too much unrequited love – high on complexity and low on fun. Fritch’s earthy and colourful style knows no bounds; it’s illimitable. www.losttribesound.com
items._cn_summary: Lost Tribe Sound 将于夏季发行William Ryan Fritch的三张专辑。Finney与说唱艺术家Matt Finney合作的《A History, In Boxes》以班卓琴为核心，融合口语诗与电声元素，呈现青春记忆与失恋创伤的美国乡土意象。《The Old Believers》扩展版则收录电影配乐，呈现古典倾向的深沉氛围，包括奥斯卡提名纪录片《4.1 Miles》的相关音乐。文本评论文字具有抒情性，强调配乐作为独立艺术作品的价值而非仅为画面服务。整体偏向美国民谣与电影配乐领域，在编曲上虽有电声跨界尝试，但核心仍属于温暖叙事性的传统美式音乐语言。

items.body: Bruno bavota has championed the piano since he first discovered its use as a musical instrument… Much of the record is populated by the dorian (bright) and mixolydian (mixed and misty) types of modes and keys. This type of playing – more whole tones than semitones (more white notes than black; less jazz notes and more classic). The corresponding metric structure of the pieces – adhering to traditional 4 and 8 bar phrases – keeps momentum. Meanwhile the tempo is a glacial coastal eddy over the waves, while with some sharper waves, always brings back to shore. It’s this light effect of all the techniques put together that creates an ennui that is long lasting and free flowing. The compositional clarion call is inclusive of strings as well, as on hugely emotive opener ‘Out Of The Blue’. The track sounds like a soundtrack to a non-sugary French or foreign film from somewhere long lost and idyllic. Comparisons can quite obviously be made to contemporary composers such as Nils Frahm and Eluvium, but there is something different here. Something out of the blue. Something forgotten. A posted note from the outlands of time. The reverse refrain aesthetic of the violins punctuating early sections of the album signify this perfectly. In the sense that instrumental levity is a beacon for change and formlessness, but solidity at the same time. One of those great paradoxes of the more that is put in, sometimes the more room for change amidst possible clutter. That is the most gorgeous thing amongst these misty tones, actually – the lack of clutter. The precision/rhythmicality. “Marea” is a slowly descending trip through G major down to E minor with a lovely sveltness to the strokes of the fingers. Additionally while pieces can be seen as quite short sometimes, the precision quality is heightened by their brevity. It is hard to pick any fault. The imagery conjured up is also bright, vivid contours of lush fauna; golden fields. Certainly not something doueur and depressing. Rather, one of those bolts from the blue. A gift from a blue skyline. www.brunobavota.com
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以钢琴为核心，融合弦乐，呈现出新古典主义风格。音乐采用多利亚和混合利底亚调式，以全音而非半音为主，营造出明亮而朦胧的色调。曲式遵循传统的4小节和8小节结构，节奏缓慢如海岸漩涡，给人悠长而自由的倦怠感。小提琴的倒影旋律贯穿专辑，象征着轻盈与变化的悖论。整体编曲简洁精准，缺乏繁杂，以简短的篇幅和精确的演奏见长。评论将其与Nils Frahm和Eluvium相提并论，但更强调一种被遗忘的、来自时间远方的声音特质。音乐意象明亮生动，金色田野与郁郁葱葱的植被，并非忧郁之作。对于偏好实验、前卫和爵士融合的听众来说，这张作品偏向传统新古典范畴，跨界融合度和创新性有限。

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�

items.body: Review by Grumpyprogfan — Quivira is the name of a road close to where I live. And with three reviewers hailing this a "masterpiece" and referencing the band Kansas - well, I had to check this out. The musicans are: Lisa LaRue, composer, keys, drum programming; John Baker, guitar, bass, vocals; Jake Livgreen, vocals; With... Joe Deninzon, violin, and Evan Stanley plays guitar on one song. The musicians are quite good and Lisa's compositions are good, but it has a Neal Morse / Flying Colors vibe more than a Kansas vibe, for me. I like that Quivira has lots of instrumental sections - where the musicians can jam - because the vocals are far from the majestic duo that was Steinhardt and Walsh. In fact, there aren't many vocals on this album at all. Overall, this is a good debut album, and if you enjoy a mostly instrumental retro 70's style of music, Quivira could be worth a listen. I'm curious is this a one-off, or is a second album with a human drummer a possibility? Solid 3.5 stars.
items._cn_summary: Quivira的首张专辑由作曲家Lisa LaRue领衔，键盘与鼓编程为核心架构，辅以吉他、贝斯和小提琴。整体风格偏向七十年代复古器乐摇滚，与Kansas和Neal Morse的路线有所关联，但更接近Flying Colors的感觉。专辑以大量器乐段落为主，留给乐手即兴jam的空间， vocal部分相对克制且不突出。编曲扎实，乐手技术良好，但缺乏明显的实验性元素和个人辨识度。对于偏好前衛实验、即兴爵士或电子跨界融合的听众而言，这张作品的风格取向较为保守，属于传统交响前卫摇滚范畴内的工整之作。

items.body: Review by ZowieZiggy — Yet another review for a Purple live album.But I still enjoy to listen and review such sort of record.My first live encounter dated from March, 1973 in Brussels. (Belgium). I was 14 years old...And the ladst one will be on October 20. 2026, in Madrid (Spain). Quite a long ride isn't it?This double CD starts with 2 killers: "Highway Star" & "Black Night".Difficult to imagine a better start! And the so afraid "karaokee" style is even forgotten during the latter. So far, so great!Two very good renditions of � tracks from "The Battle Rages On" (logical since it was released in 1993 (date of recording of this live set).then come a superb "Bethoven's Ninth"...the magic of Jon to combine classic with rock; A somptuous 10 minutes (or almost) track which brings me close to ectasy (at times!). To confirm the great shape, the great "Knocking on your Back Door" from "Perfect Strangers" adds to the general feeling. SUPERB!!!But, what to say write about the two pieces of resistance of this double CD set???"Child in Time" (from "In Rock") and the fabulous, and the best from all their live sets for "Anya".This closes CD1 that be rated as a 5* one.CD2 though will sound a little weaker.Not with "The Battle" nor "lazy" which are outstanding as well. But thereafter, the next 3 titels are shortered versions of known numbers just as on their "NEC" live. Press next. three tiems;Then, we are going to face an EXTRAordinary cover version of a mythical Stones song. My favorite of tyhis great rock band. "Paint it, Blcack". from hard rocking to spacey: it is soooo great. One of the too few highlights of disc 2.We're back on great track with "Speed King" (we can even hear some notes from "Burn" before minute 6 (only instrumental, 'cause Ian will NEVER sing sing it; nor any song from Mark 3.The last but one song is an OK version of "Hush" from Mark I...But the worse is goi,ng to happen to the overlooooong karaoke version of "Smoke on the Water".I really couldn't stand this while attending their concerts. What I did at the time, was going up to the floors and attend the bar to drink one (or two - remember, I'm Belgian) with one of my mates (hi, Jean-Pierre). It was in the Arena in Antwerp (just next door to the Sport Palace).The intro is fine (almost 3 minutes) is fine with me; As well as the core track...which leads us to minute 7.And then ...5 minutes of Smoooooooke on the Water...for about another 3 minutes.The audience might have loved this, but I didn't...Sorry guys...All in all, this is an excellent hard-rocking live album. Another one from Purple; THE MASTER, THE INVENTER of the genre.**** solid stars. .
items._cn_summary: Deep Purple 1993年斯图加特现场双CD，收录了乐队横跨多个时期的代表曲目。CD1以《Highway Star》和《Black Night》开场，并包含将古典与摇滚融合的《Bethoven's Ninth》，以及经典长曲《Child in Time》和《Anya》，整体表现强劲。CD2质量略有下滑，曲目多为短缩版，缺乏新意，亮点是滚石名曲《Paint It, Black》的出色改编以及《Speed King》尾段对《Burn》的器乐引用。然而，《Smoke on the Water》长达数分钟的卡拉OK式观众互动段落令作者感到冗长乏味。作为一场传统硬摇滚演出的记录，演奏扎实但缺乏实验性与前卫元素，更偏向怀旧与商业现场呈现。
