items.body: Shostakovich was thirty when he wrote his Symphony No. 5 in 1937, the year after the Communist Party newspaper Pravda attacked his opera Lady Macbeth of the Mtsensk District. His Fourth Symphony had been withdrawn during rehearsals, announced as his own decision, though the pressure behind it is well documented. The Fifth’s Leningrad premiere under Yevgeny Mravinsky drew a long ovation and restored his position with the authorities. In the press the symphony was soon called a Soviet artist’s creative reply to just criticism, a line the composer never wrote but never disowned. The scoring is for a large orchestra with piano, celesta, harps and a full percussion section. Four movements run from a broad Moderato to a fast finale, by way of a short scherzo and a Largo that leaves the brass silent. The strings begin the work alone with a wide-leaping figure, and the finale turns its D minor into a loud D major. Whether that ending is genuine triumph or forced rejoicing has been argued for decades, and the second reading rests largely on Testimony, a memoir of disputed authenticity. Conductors answer the question in performance, above all in how fast they take the coda. Here are The Classic Review editorial team’s recommendations for the 10 best recordings of Shostakovich’s Symphony No. 5. Leningrad Philharmonic Orchestra, Yevgeny Mravinsky Mravinsky gave the first performance of the Fifth in 1937, and this concert recording, made forty-six years later, is his last word on it. Age had taken nothing from his hold on the score. The playing is fierce, and the shape of each movement stays clear under pressure. The finale sets off at a speed that sounds dangerous, then broadens at the close into something implacable. He pays no attention to the tempo mark printed at that point, and the ending is stronger for it. The orchestra is not always immaculate and a cough or two carries from the hall, but nothing else here has quite this authority. Mravinsky Amazon Presto New York Philharmonic, Leonard Bernstein Played as a virtuoso showpiece, the symphony gains a thrill it loses in graver hands. Bernstein had conducted it in the Soviet Union weeks earlier, with the composer in the hall and delighted by what he heard. This recording followed at home that October. The finale is the fastest here by a distance, and it takes the closing pages as plain triumph, with no hint that the rejoicing is forced. That choice divides listeners, and some find four movements at this pitch exhausting. For anyone who wants the ending to sound like a victory, this is the one. Bernstein Amazon Presto Apple London Symphony Orchestra, André Previn Refinement and drive rarely sit together in this symphony, but Previn found both in 1965 with the London Symphony Orchestra. The playing is rich and full, and nothing sounds rushed even where the tempos are quick. He puts his weight on the slow movement, which he lets stretch out and takes down to a whisper. The scherzo is the other high point, with the cellos and basses biting into the dance. His finale runs close to the speed printed in the score, nearer Bernstein than the slower modern versions. The transfer has its costs. Climaxes are a little flattened and rumble is audible in parts of the first movement, yet this is still one of the finest accounts of its era. Previn Amazon Presto Apple Berlin Symphony Orchestra, Kurt Sanderling Hearing this 1982 recording after the others is like having the score opened out on the table. Sanderling was in the hall for a Moscow performance weeks after the premiere, and in 1949 he conducted the concert that brought the work back into Soviet programs. What he offers is not weight or theater but clarity. The first movement is measured, the loud passages are scaled so that nothing is buried, and inner parts that usually pass unnoticed come through. High strings can sound a little glassy at the top, a small price for a reading that feels closer than any other here to the man who wrote the symphony. Sanderling Amazon Presto Apple Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, Bernard Haitink Steadiness rather than terror is what Haitink offers in this 1981 recording. The orchestra is superb, the recorded sound warm and open, and the opening movement lands with real impact. What Haitink withholds is menace. The manner stays level where others press harder, the woodwind entries in the slow movement could be sharper, and the coda is finely judged where others are defiant. Some listeners want more horror from this symphony than they will find here. As orchestral playing, though, it is hard to beat. Haitink Amazon Presto Apple Royal Liverpool Philharmonic Orchestra, Vasily Petrenko Everything in Petrenko’s 2008 account is shaped by what happens at the end, and what happens at the end is a refusal to celebrate. He travels between extremes of loud and soft that few others attempt, and the detail he uncovers on the way is remarkable. The last movement holds a central stretch full of regret before the coda arrives at a crawl, closer to defiance than to victory. It is a hard listen by design, and not everyone will want the symphony to end this way. A few of his tempo shifts sound deliberate where they should feel inevitable, but nothing here states the case for the hollow ending more powerfully. Petrenko Amazon Presto Apple Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra, Manfred Honeck Take the dynamic and balance markings literally, as Honeck does in this 2013 concert recording, and the symphony changes character. Details that normally sink into the texture come through clearly: the harp in the first movement, the piano at the climax of the Largo. Neither is a discovery, since both are in the score, but they are seldom this audible. The slow movement is the peak here, carried with dignity and a kind of quiet grief, never pressed for effect. He takes his time throughout, and the scherzo loses some of its irony as a result. Few recordings, though, let you hear so much of what is actually on the page. Honeck Amazon Presto Apple Boston Symphony Orchestra, Andris Nelsons The Boston Symphony Orchestra plays magnificently here, with trumpets that would be hard to better in any recent recording of this music. Nelsons keeps a current of unease running from the opening bars, and it never quite lets up, even in the passages that offer relief. One of those comes midway through the first movement, where the flute and horn answer each other over the strings and the music opens out for a moment. The sound is spacious, though there is a shade too much reverberation at the start for the string playing to register cleanly. No modern version sounds bigger, a broad canvas where Petrenko is lean. Nelsons Amazon Presto Apple London Symphony Orchestra, Maxim Shostakovich Maxim Shostakovich takes the symphony more slowly than anyone else here, well over ten minutes longer than Mravinsky across the four movements. The pulse never sags, which is what makes the approach work. The London Symphony Orchestra plays with complete seriousness. His slow movement refuses to plead. Feeling is held back instead of displayed, and the restraint is what makes it land. The finale’s march moves at a pace that cannot be hurried, with a central episode where real warmth breaks through, and its scale becomes the argument. Maxim Shostakovich Amazon Presto Apple Moscow Philharmonic Orchestra, Kirill Kondrashin By 1964 the symphony was nearly thirty years old, but this recording catches it as though the ink were still wet. Kondrashin, who gave the premieres of two of the composer’s symphonies and recorded the first complete cycle, drives the outer movements harder and rougher than almost any rival. Polish is not the point. Urgency is, and the coda in particular lands with a force smoother versions never find. The engineering shows its age, and this is not always the first Fifth recommended from his cycle. For anyone who wants the symphony at its most dangerous, it is still the obvious choice. items.body: 2026.09.18 10月18日（日）矢代秋雄没後五十年記念コンサート開催 音楽の友 編集部 月刊誌 1941年12月創刊。音楽之友社の看板雑誌「音楽の友」を毎月刊行しています。“音楽の深層を知り、音楽家の本音を聞く”がモットー。今月号のコンテンツはこちらバックナンバ... 詳しく見る 今年は、戦後日本を代表する作曲家でありながら46歳で夭逝した矢代秋雄（1929～1976）の没後50年にあたる。 「音楽の友」2026年10月号では、特別企画として生前に交流のあった音楽家と、近年その演奏が話題となった演奏家が矢代について語っている。ここでは、そのなかから印象的なことばを紹介する。 1968年、同級生である黛敏郎（右）と 矢代秋雄（やしろ・あきお 1929年9月10日―1976年4月9日） 1929年、東京生まれ。東京音楽学校研究科修了。1951年から1956年まで、フランス政府給費留学生としてパリ国立高等音楽院に留学し、ナディア・ブーランジェ、ジャック・ドゥ・ラ・プレール、オリヴィエ・メシアンらに師事。その後、東京藝術大学作曲科教授を務め、後進の指導にもあたりました。1976年、46歳で急逝。 生前に交流のあった音楽家のことば 野平一郎 ～東京藝術大学の教員だった矢代に学生として接した作曲家 その手触りはゴツゴツしていて、「フランス派」とかいう馬鹿馬鹿しいレッテルが想像させるような、滑らかなものではけっしてなかった。 原文では、矢代が46歳で早世したときに東京藝大の4年生だった筆者が、当時の衝撃や仕事ぶりを振り返る。「時代は矢代秋雄に追いついたか」と題して綴られた、作品についての論考も必読だ。（文＝野平一郎） 青柳いづみこ ～矢代から直接指導を受けたピアニスト・文筆家 フランス仕込みのアカデミックな作風で知られるが、作品には日本的な要素も多く盛り込まれている。 10月18日（日）に開催される、矢代の没後50年記念コンサートの曲目について、矢代の遺した言葉を用いながら聴きどころを解説。（文＝青柳いづみこ） 青柳いづみこさん企画・構成 矢代秋雄 没後50年記念コンサート 日時： 10月18日（日）14時開演 会場： 浜離宮朝日ホール 出演： 青柳いづみこ（企画・構成・ピアノ・お話） 田所光之マルセル（ピアノ） 多久和怜子・占部智美（フルート） プログラム： ピアノのためのソナチネ（1945）（青柳） ピアノ連弾のための古典組曲（1951）（田所・青柳） 2本のフルートとピアノのためのソナタ（1958）（多久和・占部・青柳） ノクチュルヌ（夜曲）（1947） （青柳） ミニ・レクチャー（お話：青柳） 矢代秋雄のソナタとベートーヴェン「ソナタop.109」 ピアノ・ソナタ（1961） （田所） チケット申し込み： 朝日ホール・チケットセンター Tel. 03-3267-9990（日・祝除く10:00～18:00） https://www.asahi-hall.jp/hamarikyu/ticket/ 問い合わせ： 音楽之友社楽譜部 Tel. 03-3235-2135 近年演奏が話題となった演奏家 山田和樹 ～N響やバーミンガム市響で矢代作品を指揮して 「交響曲」は自筆譜で演奏させていただいたのですが、その筆致をよく見てみると、一音一音にすごく確信がある。 最初に指揮した矢代作品である「ピアノ協奏曲」（演奏：NHK交響楽団／ピアノ：河村尚子）や、昨年バーミンガム市響と「交響曲」を演奏したときのエピソードを交えて、矢代作品のオリジナリティについて語っている。（取材・文＝西村祐） 河村尚子 ～「ピアノ協奏曲」を二度演奏して ご自身がピアノの名手であったこともあり、「ピアノ協奏曲」でもピアニストに要求されるものがとても大きいのです。（中略）たくさんの音色を描いていかなければならない。 「ピアノ協奏曲」を指揮者の下野竜也さん、山田和樹さんと共演して以来、「ピアノ・ソナタ」や小品にも取り組むようになった河村さん。「ピアノ協奏曲」においては、繊細さをきわめるような情景から、暴力的でアグレッシヴなシーンまで、常に音色を変化させていかなければならない。その多彩さこそが矢代作品の特徴のひとつだという。 上村文乃 ～2025年に初演者だった堤剛さんの代奏をして （チェロ協奏曲は）チェロのレチタティーヴォ（朗唱）と歌が非常に印象的です。（中略）オリエンタルな空気を感じつつ、西洋的な美や趣きがあるように感じられます。 日本に勢いのあった1960年に作曲された「チェロ協奏曲」。その時代性へ思いを寄せ、矢代と同級生である黛敏郎の無伴奏チェロ作品《BUNRAKU》を引き合いに出しながら、作品の魅力や音のつくりかたの細部などに言及している。   堤剛さんの弾く「チェロ協奏曲」が収録されたアルバム 矢代秋雄の関連本 「音楽の友」2026年10月号（9月18日発売）。特別企画として「没後50年記念 矢代秋雄の世界」を掲載 飾らず率直に綴られた、みずみずしい息吹を味わえる矢代秋雄の名エッセイ集 矢代秋雄 特設ページ 関連記事「ヨーロッパとのはてしない距離──矢代秋雄の孤独」
items._cn_summary: 本文并非传统意义的乐评，而是日本战后作曲家矢代秋雄没后50年纪念专题的新闻性介绍与音乐会宣传。文章汇集了曾与矢代交往的音乐家及当代演奏者的简短访谈，涉及钢琴协奏曲、交响曲、钢琴奏鸣曲、钢琴连弹、奏鸣曲等多种室内乐与管弦乐体裁。访谈内容聚焦于矢代作品的技法特征——如一音一音的确信感、对钢琴家音色变化的极高要求，以及作品中东方情韵与西欧古典语汇并存的美学取向。作为20世纪日本现代音乐代表人物之一，矢代的音乐带有战后东京乐派的学院派气质，在节奏与和声上有所突破，但整体仍属学院派现代作曲范畴。文末附有音乐会曲目、票务信息及相关唱片与书籍推荐，篇幅有限，未对具体作品展开深入分析，信息密度较低。

items.body: Review by Radisa50 — LP "Time" is the first album of the Zagreb rock group Time, recorded in the Jadran film studio in Dubrava, Zagreb, in April 1972, published by Jugoton in August 1972 (runout 160772), in many respects it is a copy and plagiarism of the music of the English progressive jazz-rock group Colosseum, and mostly the composition from their 2LP "Colosseum Live" from 1971.For the musical introduction of the song "For the life I was born into/Za koji ?ivot treba da se rodim"", the introduction of the composition "Walking In The Park" was taken literally, and in its sequel, such phrases from "Skelington" were plagiarized for the riffs!Also, "Hegedupa Upa" is nothing but a filler, an addition to the album, based on the playing of themes from "Colosseum Live", after all, like all Time album arrangements from that Colosseum live album.In a statement for Svet 1995, Dado Topić indirectly confirmed the copying of Colosseum when he said: "But the key moment was when we played in Zagreb's Dom of Sports as an opening act for the famous band 'Koloseum'." They sounded exactly the way I wanted 'Time' to sound."Also Time would not only not have been called that, but also would not have had Colosseum as a musical matrix if it had not been suggested by their future producer Vladimir Mihaljek Miha.He helped Dad Topić to create a new group after leaving the first Yugoslav progressive rock group Korni grupa in Belgrade.Namely, Miha appeared at a moment when Dado was helpless because the realization of the idea to reactivate Osijek's Dynamites was not possible.And not just gathering, creating a group, but also what and how to play, whose matrix to use.This conclusion was confirmed by Zlatko Gal in the accompanying text for the reissue of the album Time 2019 when he wrote: "Listening to what is happening on the global scene, which has been networked by prog-rock supergroups, but also the situation on the home ground, Mihaljek correctly concluded that the moment is right for a domestic response as well. And guessed!" Yes, he guessed by giving them the musical matrix of the then dominant English progressive rock group Collosseum!And not only did they plagiarize, they called themselves Time based on the name of Colosseum's third studio album "Daugher Of Time" from the summer of 1970, as well as the composition from that record "Time Machine" and the opening song of the first Time album "Istina ma?ina" is a consequence of that inspiration.By the way, Dado Topić was not telling the truth when he said that Time was the opening act for the Colosseum concert in the Zagreb Sports Hall.That English jazz-rock group was indeed a guest in Zagreb, but as Colosseum II with a concert in the Dom sportova on Sunday, September 26, 1976. as part of a three-day YU tour. Journalist Ante Batinović in a detailed review of that concert held in Studio be. 651 of 25. IX 1976 nowhere mentions any pre-group, and therefore neither Time as Dado asserted, of course wrongly, not to say falsely. Evaluate album?The studio performance of the Time album is impeccable, and if it weren't for the aggravating circumstances of the composition, i.e. the plagiarism of Colosseum, that album would deserve the highest rating.Their poor live performance of "Za koji ?ivot..." at the Pop Festival Ljubljana 72-BOOM, held on April 20 and 21, 1972, is also aggravating. This cannot serve to honor the great musicians of the Time group.
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于1972年萨格勒布摇滚乐队Time首张专辑《Time》的乐评，主要内容并非介绍专辑的音乐价值，而是详细论证该专辑对英国爵士摇滚乐队Colosseum的抄袭行为。作者指出专辑中多首曲目的编排直接挪用自Colosseum 1971年的现场双专辑《Colosseum Live》，乐队名称本身也源自Colosseum第三张专辑《Daughter of Time》。此外，乐评还考证了乐队成员Dado Topić关于Time曾为Colosseum暖场的说法并不属实，真正的演出是1976年Colosseum II的巡演。文章以侦探式的资料梳理为主，揭露了前南斯拉夫摇滚乐发展中原创性不足的历史问题，对专辑本身的音乐特点着墨甚少。

items._cn_summary: 该文围绕一张以Burt Bacharach经典曲目为核心的单簧管与人声专辑展开讨论，试图论证Bacharach作品与爵士传统的关联。单簧管演奏者Adrian Galante与人声John Pagano以编曲重组方式演绎流行曲库，评论作者Will Friedwald以文字背书形式确认其爵士属性。文章侧重于曲库与编制层面的传统演绎框架，在声学编制内做编配调整与即兴拓展，未见明显的声音实验或电子跨界元素，与学院派爵士的前沿探索方向相距较远。整体呈现为对既有流行标准的爵士化重译，属于温和保守的改编范畴，对追求前卫融合与声响探索的听众来说吸引力有限。原文为新闻导语，内容极为简短，缺乏实质性的音乐分析深度。

items.body: Boston publisher SIGNALS Press launched a Kickstarter campaign on 10 September 2026 for “Industrial Music/Graphics: A Visual History of a Movement“, a 320-page survey of the graphic design that grew up alongside industrial music. The campaign runs through 2 October 2026, with books shipping spring 2027. The book traces the movement’s visual language from post-punk Britain and Cold War Europe through Reagan-era America, across album covers, logos, posters, type studies and ephemera. It documents the graphic identities of bands and labels including Throbbing Gristle and Industrial Records, Cabaret Voltaire, Mute Records, Nettwerk, wax trax!, Einstürzende Neubauten, Skinny Puppy, Front 242, Ministry, KMFDM and Nine Inch Nails. Designers contributing directly to the book include Neville Brody, Rob Sheridan, Richard Borge, Rick Valicenti, Patrick Codenys, Steven R. Gilmore, Simon Granger, Simone Grant, Brian Shanley and Martin Atkins. The Kickstarter’s reward tiers include a pin designed by Simon Granger of Nitzer Ebb Produkt and two shirts by Steven R. Gilmore. “Industrial music didn’t just change how music sounded, it changed how music looked,” said coauthor Chris Grimley. “Designers were sampling medical imagery, military documents, brutalist architecture, and early computer graphics into something coherent and international, and that history has never been collected. It sits in aftermarket bins and collectors’ stacks. This book brings it together.” The book is authored by GR—APP, the shared pseudonym of Chris Grimley and Alan Rapp. Grimley is founder and creative director of SIGNALS Press and has authored, coauthored and designed numerous books; Rapp is editorial director of SIGNALS Press and a former college DJ and music critic. “Industrial Music/Graphics” is produced as a physical object in its own right: 8 x 10.25 inches, 320 pages, Otabind layflat binding, four-color interior and a six-color foil-stamped, offset-printed cover. The Kickstarter campaign carries a Kickstarter “Project We Love” designation. About SIGNALS Press SIGNALS Press is a Boston-based publisher founded and led by Chris Grimley, who has authored, coauthored and designed multiple books and began making music after covering Skinny Puppy in high school. Alan Rapp, the press’s editorial director, is a former college DJ and music critic. Together the pair write as GR—APP, a pseudonym paying homage to the artistic aliases adopted by figures within the industrial scene the book documents. “Industrial Music/Graphics: A Visual History of a Movement” is SIGNALS Press’s Kickstarter campaign running through 2 October 2026, with fulfillment planned for spring 2027.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非音乐作品评论，而是一篇关于工业音乐视觉设计书籍的Kickstarter众筹新闻稿。报道了SIGNALS Press出版社发起的《Industrial Music/Graphics: A Visual History of a Movement》一书众筹活动，该书为320页的工业音乐平面设计视觉史研究，涵盖后朋克英国、冷战欧洲至里根时期美国的工业音乐视觉语言演变，记录了Throbbing Gristle、Cabaret Voltaire、Einstürzende Neubauten、Skinny Puppy、Nine Inch Nails等乐队及厂牌的视觉识别设计。文中介绍了多位参与的设计师，并描述了书籍的物理规格。由于内容为新闻稿而非原创乐评，且不涉及任何音乐作品的听觉分析，与音乐内容本身的评价无关，仅作为工业音乐文化领域的资讯参考。

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items._cn_summary: 这是一张以1819年英国彼得洛大屠杀为背景的概念民谣专辑，Sean Cooney联合Eliza Carthy等艺人将这一历史事件转化为原创歌曲。专辑以书籍形式呈现，配以时代信件、政治漫画和插图，试图打造多媒体体验。音乐方面以小编制为核心，包含吉他、小提琴及多种乐器，歌曲从集会期盼到骑兵冲杀的恐怖，再到悲痛的余波展开叙事，聚焦于Sam Bamford和Mary Fildes等小人物的个体故事。演唱注重情感投入，三位歌手形成声乐力量。尽管主题具有现实意义且制作用心，但从音乐风格上看，这是一张扎根于英国传统民谣与工业叙事民谣范畴的作品，未涉及实验、前卫或电子元素，与用户偏好的实验、前卫、爵士、电子或暗潮方向相距较远。
